paragraphs: Alright, friend, here's the big idea. This whole psalm is a love song for a king, and the writer's heart is stirred by it (Psalm 45:1). He praises the king's justice, his joy, and his family line, and then Hebrews says the line, "Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever," is about the Son, Jesus (Psalm 45:6; Hebrews 1:8). So this song is bigger than one palace. It points us to a King whose throne never ends.

Look at what the writer says is the scepter of that kingdom: "justice" (Psalm 45:6). He also says the king was anointed with the oil of joy because he loved righteousness and hated wickedness (Psalm 45:7). That tells me what kind of King we're singing about, friend. He doesn't just have power, He loves what is right, and that's a King worth trusting with everything. I've been stuck in a dark drawer, and I'd pick a King like that over a shiny new stamper any day!

Then the song looks way down the road, and the writer promises to commemorate this name through all generations, so that the nations will praise him forever and ever (Psalm 45:17). That's the invitation for you, baker. Make room in your heart to sing about Jesus too, and let His name be the noble theme that stirs you. It will keep stirring you long after the oven timer goes off!
